history.period: Modern ISKCON centre; founding year not documented
history.summary: The ISKCON temple at Ambicapatti (Ambica Patty), Silchar, is a Gaudiya Vaishnava centre of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness founded on the teachings of Srila Prabhupada. The temple stands close to 50 feet tall and enshrines Sri Sri Radha Krishna along with Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. It is a prominent landmark known for daily kirtans, Mangala Aarti, Bhagavad Gita and Srimad Bhagavatam classes, free vegetarian prasad distribution, and charitable work in the Barak Valley. No documented construction date was found for the Silchar centre — do not invent one.

name: ISKCON Silchar
town_description: Silchar is the headquarters of Cachar district in southern Assam's Barak Valley, on the banks of the Barak (Surma) River. A predominantly Bengali-speaking commercial and educational hub, it is the gateway to Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura, served by an airport, railway station, and national highways.

travel.airport: Silchar Airport (Kumbhirgram, IXS), about 20 km away
travel.railway: Silchar Railway Station (SCL), about 2-3 km away
travel.road: Ambicapatti neighbourhood in central Silchar; reachable by auto-rickshaw and city transport

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; during Janmashtami and Rath Yatra for the biggest celebrations
visitor_information.opening_hours: One travel source lists 9:30 AM to 10:00 PM, Monday to Saturday, closed Sunday — this pattern is unusual for an ISKCON temple and should be verified locally before visiting.
